sections.heading: Swagatika Swain vs State Of Odisha ..... Opposite Party on 12 September, 2024
Bench: Aditya Kumar Mohapatra
content: 01. 1. This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the State-Opposite Party. Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with C.T. Case No.1997 of 2023, arising out of CID Cyber Crime P.S. Case No.33 of 2023, pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Bhubaneswar, for alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 409 / 465 / 467 / 468 / 469 / 471 /120B/ 34 of Page 1 of 4. I.P.C . read with Section 66 & 66C of Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008.

4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner is in custody since 31.03.2024. He further contended that in the meantime investigation has been concluded and final charge sheet has been filed. Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that the Petitioner, who was working as an employee of the ICICI Bank, has been implicated in the present case on the allegation of misappropriating bank's money to the tune of Rs.1,04,58,647/-. He further submitted that initially an F.I.R. was registered for the self-same allegation vide Dhenkanal Town P.S. Case No.138 of 2023. In the said case, the Petitioner has already been enlarged on anticipatory bail vide order dated 01.11.2023 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.8954 of 2023. Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that on the self-same occurrence, the present case has been registered on 5.12.2023 bearing F.I.R. No.33 by the Cyber Crime Police Station for alleged commission of offences under Sections 409 / 465 / 467 / 468 / 471 / 120-B / 34 of the I.P.C. read with Sections 66 / 66C of the Information Technology Act. Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that the Petitioner, who is a lady, is required to be looked after her young kids. He further contended that since the offences alleged are all triable Magistrate and that in the meantime investigation has been concluded and charge sheet has been filed. Therefore, the Page 2 of 4. Petitioner be released on bail in any terms and conditions which the Petitioner shall abide by while on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that allegation made against the Petitioner in F.I.R. are grave and serious in nature. He further contended that allegation involves misappropriation of public money while she was working in the private sector bank. He further contended that in the event the Petitioner is released on bail there is every likelihood that she might abscond from justice which would cause delay in conclusion of the trial.

6. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on a careful examination of the materials on record and further taking note of the fact that the offences alleged are all triable by Magistrate and that in the meantime charge sheet has been filed and keeping in view the period of custodial detention, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail.

7. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case by the Court in seisin over the matter on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper. The release of the Petitioner shall also be subject to the conditions that she shall appear before the trial court on each and every date of posting of the case; she shall not threaten/influence/gain over any of the prosecution witnesses or shall not make any attempt to tamper with the prosecution evidence in any manner Page 3 of 4. whatsoever while on bail; she shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court in seisin over the matter without prior permission of the Court in seisin over the matter; and while on bail, she shall not leave the country and surrender her travel documents like passport etc. before Court in seisin over the matter. In the event the Petitioner does not have any travel document, she shall file an affidavit to that effect before the Court in seisin over the matter. Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
8. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
( A.K. Mohapatra ) Judge Debasis Signature Not Verified Digitally Signed Signed by: DEBASIS AECH Reason: Authentication Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT Date: 13-Sep-2024 10:51:49 Page 4 of 4.
